subtype: Adult child seeing a parent low or anxious [Actor]
passage: Yusuf, I heard you on the phone with your father just now. Can I tell you something from my own life? When I was about your age, my Appa retired and then just faded. He stopped reading the newspaper. He sat on the balcony till dark and barely spoke at meals. I was the one living at home, so I quietly took over: the bills, his tablets, the cooking, even reminding him to bathe. I felt I had become his parent, and I was frightened and guilty all the time, because I was angry too. My brothers in the city had no idea. One night I finally phoned them and said, "I can't do this alone." That weekend all three of us sat with Appa and said, "We love you. You don't seem yourself. Let's see Dr Rao together." He grumbled, but he went. It helped him, slowly. And it helped me more than I can say. I'm Uma, and I wish I'd called them sooner.

qa.q: Where did Uma's Appa sit till dark?
What did Uma feel while quietly taking over everything?
qa.a: Uma felt frightened and guilty, and angry too, as if Uma had become Appa's parent.

qa.q: What was the turning point for Uma?
qa.a: Phoning the brothers and saying "I can't do this alone", which led all three to speak lovingly with Appa and take him to Dr Rao.

qa.q: How might Appa have felt when all three children sat with him?
qa.a: He may have felt embarrassed, hence the grumbling, but also loved and less alone, which is why he agreed to go.

grounding: It shows an older person recalling seeing a father withdraw, feeling role reversal, fear and guilt, and choosing to share the load with siblings and suggest a doctor.

subtype: Adult child seeing a parent low or anxious [Actor]
passage: Ammi called Parveen four times before noon, as she did most days now. Had Parveen reached work? Was the gas off at home? Had Nadeem's train arrived safely? On the crowded station platform, Parveen could barely hear her over the announcements. Ammi's voice was thin and fast, and she said she hadn't slept properly since Abbu's operation. Parveen felt her chest tighten. Somewhere in the last year she had started parenting her own mother, and it frightened her. She also felt guilty for being irritated by the calls. That night she texted her brother Nadeem: "Ammi isn't okay. I've been handling it alone and I can't. Can we both talk to her on Sunday?" On Sunday, squeezed onto Ammi's bed, they held her hands. "Ammi, we love you. This much worry is hard on your health. Will you come with us to Dr Mathew?" Ammi cried, then nodded. Nadeem booked the visit; Parveen promised to come too.

qa.q: How many times did Ammi call before noon?
What two feelings did Parveen have about Ammi's calls?
qa.a: Fear at having started to parent her own mother, and guilt at feeling irritated by the calls.

qa.q: Which choice changed things, and why?
qa.a: Parveen stopped handling it alone and asked Nadeem to talk to Ammi together, so the load was shared and Ammi was gently steered to a doctor.

qa.q: How might Ammi feel when both children held her hands?
qa.a: She may feel loved and seen rather than scolded, which is why she cried and then agreed to see Dr Mathew.

grounding: It shows a young woman seeing her mother constantly worried, feeling role reversal, fear and guilt, and speaking with love and her brother to suggest a doctor visit.
